The loser recovers by
its mode's own discipline --- an in-band rotation in mode 1, a later
scheduled generation in mode 2, the next lockstep switch in mode 3 ---
at the price of its missed slots (operational discipline; mode 1's half
is also checked in the core, \code{liveness\_produce\_blockK}).
lean_statement:
@MoltPetit.Model.liveness_produce_blockK : ∀ {n Δconf me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex : ℕ}
  {bad : MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineSlots} {record : MoltPetit.Model.SlotRecord} {c : MoltPetit.Model.Chain}
  {tip : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
  MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineBounded n bad →
    MoltPetit.Model.validChainK n c = true →
      List.getLast? c = some tip →
        tip.slot < slot →
          MoltPetit.Model.producerForSlot n slot = me →
            (∀ (s : ℕ), ∀ B ∈ record s, B.slot = s) →
              (∀ (u : ℕ),
                  tip.slot + 1 < u + n →
                    u + n ≤ slot + 1 →
                      MoltPetit.Model.HonestBlocksCover bad record
                        (c ++ [MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip]) u n) →
                MoltPetit.Model.keyFloor n c me ≤ keyIndex →
                  MoltPetit.Model.produceBlock? n me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex c =
                      some (MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip) ∧
                    MoltPetit.Model.validChainK' n Δconf
                        (c ++ [MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip]) =
                      true

tex_statement:
A client that misses its cadence must stop acting and re-join from a
fresh trusted checkpoint, exactly as if it were new --- operational
discipline the theorems force rather than state: past the cadence the
theorems' fault-budget assumption becomes one no deployment can stand
behind --- quiet thefts accumulate until nothing satisfies it
(\code{no\_budget\_beyond}), and re-joining is a fresh trust event
outside the formal development.

(Mode 3's guarantees hold at the certificate presentation as well as for
full chains (\code{lockstep\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}).

    ∀ {rosterGen : ℕ → ℕ} {Sig sk pk : Type} {ops : MoltPetit.Model.SigOps Sig sk pk}

      {honestSigned : ℕ → ℕ → Option MoltPetit.Model.Block} {now Δ : ℕ} {G : MoltPetit.Model.Block} {R T : ℕ},
      MoltPetit.Model.LockstepPackage n rosterGen ops registry rented Stolen honestSigned now Δ G R T →

          MoltPetit.Model.GroundedCertLock n (MoltPetit.Model.SignedDeclared n ops registry) G cl g →

              ∀ {s₁ s₁' : MoltPetit.Model.Block} {srest srest' : MoltPetit.Model.Chain}

                (s₁ :: srest).getLast? = some sTip →
                  (s₁' :: srest').getLast? = some sTip' →
                    s₁.height = cl.tipHeight + 1 ∧ cl.tipSlot < s₁.slot ∧ s₁.prev = some cl.tipId →
                      MoltPetit.Model.linksOk (s₁ :: srest) = true →
                        (∀ (u : ℕ),

tex_statement:
Accept a certified
chain only if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the certificate verifies (\code{CertOps.verify} --- one cheap check,
  e.g.\ of a recursive proof);
\item every suffix block's signature verifies under
  $\mathit{keyFor}(\text{slot's producer},\ \text{declared version})$;
\item the first suffix block extends the claim's tip: height one up, slot
  strictly later, \code{prev} equal to the tip id --- and every adjacent
  suffix pair links the same way;
\item every window that matures within the suffix is dense, counted over
  the claim's boundary buffer plus the suffix (\code{validSuffix});
\item the key-version discipline holds: a producer's declared versions
  never decrease (\code{keyMonoOk}, Section~\ref{sec:protocol}), and
  every block's declared version satisfies the deployment's rotation
  \emph{pin} (a floor in modes 1--2, exact per grid window in mode 3) --- the
  one mode-specific check, fixed at deployment.

\begin{theorem}[Recent chains share their deep blocks; Lean
\code{light\_client\_safety}]\label{thm:lc}
Fix $n \ge 1$, a deployment genesis, and a verifier clock $\mathit{now}$.
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:budget}--\ref{ass:cert} hold with the
$n$-slot recency rule. Take any two certified chains accepted by the
validator of Section~\ref{sec:rules}, both with recent tips
($\mathit{now} \le \mathit{tip.slot} + n$). Then any block of the first
chain's suffix with at least $n$ blocks above it equals the second
chain's block at the same height, whenever the second chain's suffix
exposes that height with $n$ blocks above it too. In particular, all
recent accepted chains agree on their common prefix up to $n$ blocks
below the lower tip, at every height both presentations expose.
\end{theorem}

(\code{TimedExecution}) adds a real-time axis: a log of what each real
slot's producer signed --- at an honest real slot, at most its own
current block; at a bad real slot, arbitrarily many blocks of the
adversary's choosing under that producer's key --- arbitrary content,

\begin{theorem}[Forged suffixes advance at half speed; Lean
\code{forged\_time\_bound}]\label{thm:forge}
In the timed model with the fault budget: let a valid chain be available
at real slot $r_{\mathrm{now}}$, let $F$ be one of its blocks, first
signed at real slot $r_0$, and let every chain block past $F$'s slot have
been signed only at bad real slots (the suffix above $F$ is forged by
coercion). Then
\[
\quorum \cdot \left\lfloor
  \tfrac{\mathit{tip.slot} - F.\mathit{slot}}{n} \right\rfloor
\;\le\;
\fmax \cdot \left( \left\lfloor \tfrac{r_{\mathrm{now}} - r_0}{n}
  \right\rfloor + 1 \right).
\]
Since $\quorum \approx 2\fmax$: forging a suffix that spans $s$ slots
takes about $2s$ real slots. The from-genesis corollary
(\code{forged\_chain\_time\_bound}) reads: a fully forged chain claiming
tip slot $s$ cannot exist before real slot ${\approx}\,2s$. (The Lean
statements carry non-degeneracy side conditions --- $n \ge 2$, $F$ not
the first block; a forged span under one window makes the
bound trivially true, ruling nothing out.)
\end{theorem}

exists) forces that middle block's first signing back to $r$ as well ---
under a key that real slot cannot reach.

slots}, each time taking as its anchor the block $n$ deep below the
newly verified tip. Suppose the key-stealing surface and hash

accepted, recent chains longer than $n$ blocks that both contain the
anchor agree: at equal tip heights, on the block $n$ below each tip; at

\begin{theorem}[Liveness; Lean \code{production\_liveness},
\code{global\_liveness}]\label{thm:live}
\emph{Local:} under the fault budget and honest delivery
(Assumptions~\ref{ass:budget} and~\ref{ass:delivery}), when a slot
arrives that belongs to an honest producer holding an accepted chain,
production succeeds --- the extension passes the same validator everyone
runs. \emph{Global:} a synchronous honest run within the budget (over
the run's span; each honest block reaches the next honest producer
within its slot) is
validator-accepted with one block per honest slot, so the chain reaches
any height and every block eventually becomes $n$-deep.
\end{theorem}
lean_statement:
@MoltPetit.Model.liveness_produce_block : ∀ {n me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex : ℕ}
  {bad : MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineSlots} {record : MoltPetit.Model.SlotRecord} {c : MoltPetit.Model.Chain}
  {tip : MoltPetit.Model.Block},
  MoltPetit.Model.ByzantineBounded n bad →
    MoltPetit.Model.validChain n c = true →
      List.getLast? c = some tip →
        tip.slot < slot →
          MoltPetit.Model.producerForSlot n slot = me →
            (∀ (s : ℕ), ∀ B ∈ record s, B.slot = s) →
              (∀ (u : ℕ),
                  tip.slot + 1 < u + n →
                    u + n ≤ slot + 1 →
                      MoltPetit.Model.HonestBlocksCover bad record
                        (c ++ [MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip]) u n) →
                MoltPetit.Model.produceBlock? n me slot newId contentsHash keyIndex c =
                  some (MoltPetit.Model.nextBlock slot newId contentsHash keyIndex tip)
